title: Cell competence lets neural-less novel aggregates self-organize functionally

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cell competence lets neural-less novel aggregates self-organize functionally

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The behavioural competence of individual cells and their propensity to cooperate in groups facilitate functional morphogenesis in novel circumstances, so that the designed organisms, despite lacking nervous systems, following novel developmental trajectories and mixing tissues, still possess self-organizing properties that support their designed behaviour.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The behavioral competence of individual cells, and the propensity of cells to cooperate in groups, facilitate functional morphogenesis in novel circumstances. The lifeforms presented here, despite lacking nervous systems, following novel developmental trajectories, and being composed of materials from different tissues, nevertheless possess these self-organizing properties.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Kriegman S, Blackiston D, Levin M, Bongard J, “A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms”, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (2020), doi:10.1073/pnas.1910837117; section “Discussion”. Scope: Xenopus cells in novel, designed multicellular configurations

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2020-xenobots-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Some consequences, such as robust shape formation and coordinated behavior, are measurable. The mechanism attribution is underdetermined by the existing small set of constructed organisms and would require stronger perturbation controls for full resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Operationalize competence as restoration of morphology or function after controlled construction variability, and cooperation as performance exceeding predictions from independent-cell behavior; compare designed aggregates with dissociated or coordination-impaired controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Competence and cooperation have multiple non-equivalent definitions.

Available observations do not isolate cell-level cooperation from ordinary tissue mechanics.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.62
data existence: 0.5
data adequacy: 0.35
discriminating power: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Maintenance of designed behavior in a novel configuration is observable and is described in the published builds. Attributing that outcome to behavioral competence and cooperation, rather than to the mechanics of adhesion and contraction, has no measurement that would come apart from those mechanics. Public materials can speak to the outcome and leave the causal wording underdetermined.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Score whether novel, nerve-free, mixed-tissue builds maintain the designed behavior and external shape; competence-as-cause would require that outcome to survive only when a separate, pre-registered measure of cell-level cooperation is intact.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Biophysical self-assembly predicts the same maintenance of shape and movement.

No deposited dataset records a cell-level competence variable separate from the organism-level behavior.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.4
data existence: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.4
discriminating power: 0.3
